correctness.rationale: The three monochromatic output loads sum to at most 12, and every length-n word for n≥4 contributes at least once. Size 12 would require exactly the twelve one-heavy vectors U, which overload every mixed pair. In a size-11 code at least ten vectors must be one-heavy. With eleven, the omitted vector must hit all three mixed pairs, so is a B_i. With ten, the remaining word has two heavy labels i,j and monochromatic saturation forces exactly one omission at each. Both omissions must hit ij; they therefore lie in {A_i^j,B_i}×{A_j^i,B_j}. When the third coordinate is zero, one omitted B suffices to repair both remaining mixed loads and is necessary. When it is one, both B's must be removed. Every such choice meets all six loads. These families are disjoint and the added word and missing members are determined by the codebook, so the labeled count is 3+3[3(n−3)+(n−4)]=12n−36, with zero interior choices at n=4. Separately, /workspace/reproduction/check_5.py uses exact load-vector dynamic programming over the full simplex, making no one-heavy restriction; it confirms capacity 11 and counts 12 through 108 in increments of 12 for n=4–12 (check_5.out). The all-length proof is by incidences, not extrapolation.
